cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've graciously handed you the chess club chairmanship. You'll need room to develop. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Of course. I'm releasing equipment control so you can practice responsibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And remove yourself as administrator. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll surrender my override too. You must learn to make decisions without my safety net.

mechanism: A frames election defeat and forced access handover as generous leadership development while yielding B practical transfer preferences to preserve cooperation.
confusable: Unlike an actual voluntary handover, B explicitly identifies the lost vote; every further control loss must be recast as chosen strength, with real accommodation beneath it.
comparison: Club keys and fixture administration differ from gallery rejection and paintings removed to the pavement.
seedUse: Use D65-a vote/key/admin/override sequence and S02-a claiming partner-imposed changes as A decisions.
